findings.highlight: The conversation was with a newspaper company we've known for a long time, but it seems that their management has changed, so I had to spend the whole day explaining things.
findings.evidenceJa: いつも付き合いのある雑誌社からだったけど、担当が替わったらしく、色々と話が通らず、つい長電話になってしまった。
findings.explanation: A familiar magazine publisher calls, but its individual contact person has changed, so mutual understanding is poor and the call runs long. The English turns the publisher into a newspaper company, the contact into management, and a long late-night call into a whole day of explanation.
findings.japanese:
いつも付き合いのある雑誌社からだったけど、
担当が替わったらしく、色々と話が通らず、
つい長電話になってしまった。
findings.todokanai: The conversation was with a newspaper company we've known for a long time, but it seems that their management has changed, so I had to spend the whole day explaining things.

findings.highlight: Not that I don't do that in my free time anyway.
findings.evidenceJa: それこそ下着を穿くのだって、下手すりゃマネージャーにやらせようとするくらい。…いや、脱がす方なら普通にやるんだけど。
findings.explanation: Haruki says Kazusa might even make her manager put her underwear on, then corrects himself: taking it off is something he routinely does. The English leaves 'that' directionless and loses the reversal from caretaking to sex that makes the punchline.
findings.japanese:
それこそ下着を穿くのだって、
下手すりゃマネージャーにやらせようとするくらい。
…いや、脱がす方なら普通にやるんだけど。
findings.todokanai: Sometimes she even makes her manager put on her underwear for her… Not that I don't do that in my free time anyway.

findings.highlight: You already know I'm the most clingy person in the world.
findings.evidenceJa: 「答えのわかってる質問をするな。あたしが世界一の甘党だってこと、世界一知ってるくせに」
findings.explanation: After Haruki asks whether she dislikes being spoiled (甘やかす), Kazusa says he knows better than anyone that she is the world's greatest 甘党—literally sweet tooth, figuratively addicted to his sweetness/indulgence. 'Most clingy person' removes the lexical joke and changes liking to be spoiled into initiating attachment.
findings.japanese:
「答えのわかってる質問をするな。
あたしが世界一の甘党だってこと、
世界一知ってるくせに」
findings.todokanai: "Don't ask questions you know the answer to. You already know I'm the most clingy person in the world."

findings.highlight: the only people the European branch consists of is the pianist herself, and her sole manager, just like in Japan.
findings.evidenceJa: それ以来、株式会社冬馬曜子オフィス欧州支部は、一人の所属アーティストと一人のマネージャーという、日本人のみの最小構成で稼動してる。
findings.explanation: The European branch operates in the smallest possible all-Japanese configuration: one represented artist and one manager. The English invents a comparison 'just like in Japan' and omits both the nationality point and deliberate minimality.
findings.japanese:
それ以来、株式会社冬馬曜子オフィス欧州支部は、
一人の所属アーティストと一人のマネージャーという、
日本人のみの最小構成で稼動してる。
findings.todokanai: Since then, the only people the European branch consists of is the pianist herself, and her sole manager, just like in Japan.

findings.highlight: By the way, that sole pianist with the household name "Touma Kazusa" attempted to replace it with her new real name.
findings.evidenceJa:
ちなみに昨年、その唯一の所属アーティストは、
冬馬かずさという“芸名”を、
“新しい本名”に合わせようとした。
findings.explanation: Touma Kazusa is explicitly her stage name, which she tried to align with her new legal name; 'household name' is an unsuitable rendering — The next line's business insistence on retaining Touma makes the surname conflict recoverable.
findings.japanese:
ちなみに昨年、その唯一の所属アーティストは、
冬馬かずさという“芸名”を、
“新しい本名”に合わせようとした。
findings.todokanai: By the way, that sole pianist with the household name "Touma Kazusa" attempted to replace it with her new real name.

findings.highlight: she attended a lecture in Hokkaido just last month… One about sea urchins, salmon roe, crabs and scallops apparently.
findings.evidenceJa: 「ああ、元気いっぱいみたいだぞ。先月北海道に講演に行ってきたんだってさ。…ウニとイクラとカニとホタテの話ばかりだけど」
findings.explanation: Youko went to Hokkaido to give a lecture; her message to them merely talks incessantly about the seafood she ate. The English makes her an attendee at a seafood lecture, reversing her professional role and missing the cover-story joke later exposed at the hospital.
findings.japanese:
「ああ、元気いっぱいみたいだぞ。
先月北海道に講演に行ってきたんだってさ。
…ウニとイクラとカニとホタテの話ばかりだけど」
findings.todokanai: "Yeah, she seems to be doing just fine. She says she attended a lecture in Hokkaido just last month… One about sea urchins, salmon roe, crabs and scallops apparently."

findings.highlight: we reach out our fingers and wipe off each other's tears, and heal our invisible wounds.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちは、お互いそのことを何も話したりしない。ただ、相手の涙を指で拭いたり、舌先で舐め取ったり、そうやって、見えない傷を舐めて癒しあう。
findings.explanation: Haruki and Kazusa silently wipe one another's tears with their fingers or lick them away with the tips of their tongues, literally enacting the idiom of licking each other's wounds. The English deletes the tongue contact and therefore the physicalized wordplay.
findings.japanese:
俺たちは、お互いそのことを何も話したりしない。
ただ、相手の涙を指で拭いたり、舌先で舐め取ったり、
そうやって、見えない傷を舐めて癒しあう。
findings.todokanai: The two of us never talk about it. Instead, we reach out our fingers and wipe off each other's tears, and heal our invisible wounds.

findings.highlight: We still refuse to talk about that country.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちはまだ、あの国のことを口に出せずにいる。
findings.explanation: Two years later they remain unable to bring themselves to speak about Japan. 'Refuse' gives them a deliberate, controlled choice where the source describes traumatic incapacity.
findings.japanese: 俺たちはまだ、あの国のことを口に出せずにいる。
findings.todokanai: We still refuse to talk about that country.

findings.highlight: A few dozen files appear on my download bar.
findings.evidenceJa: 数十メガのファイルがディスクのアクセスランプとともに流れ込んでいく。
findings.explanation: A single file tens of megabytes in size streams onto the disk as its access light flickers. The English invents several dozen files and a download bar.
findings.japanese:
数十メガのファイルが
ディスクのアクセスランプとともに流れ込んでいく。
findings.todokanai: A few dozen files appear on my download bar.

findings.highlight: The girl who makes me repress her in my heart so that my words don't leak from my mouth
findings.evidenceJa: 口から漏れない分、心の中に溜まり込み、今でも鮮明に、二年前の姿形を思い起こせる、彼女。
findings.explanation: Because Haruki never lets Setsuna's name escape his mouth, thoughts of her accumulate inside his heart. The English reverses the causal direction and makes Setsuna the agent forcing him to repress her so that he will not speak.
findings.japanese:
口から漏れない分、心の中に溜まり込み、
今でも鮮明に、二年前の姿形を思い起こせる、彼女。
findings.todokanai: The girl who makes me repress her in my heart so that my words don't leak from my mouth, the girl whose figure is still vivid in my mind two years later.

findings.highlight: You've breathed your last, Ogiso Setsuna
findings.evidenceJa: 「そうそう。何かと言えば『打倒、小木曽雪菜！』ってさ。そのためなら誰を陥れても構わないみたいな」
findings.explanation: Tomo's old slogan was 'Defeat Ogiso Setsuna!' or 'Down with Ogiso Setsuna!'—a melodramatic rivalry cry. 'You've breathed your last' converts it into a death threat and wildly escalates the recalled school hostility.
findings.japanese:
「そうそう。
何かと言えば『打倒、小木曽雪菜！』ってさ。
そのためなら誰を陥れても構わないみたいな」
findings.todokanai: "Right, right! She'd say things like, 'You've breathed your last, Ogiso Setsuna' and wouldn't mind tricking anyone to put her down."
